subject.title: Durable Core PR 1/6: define the residual-gap RFC

question: Should OpenClaw introduce a shared residual durable-runtime layer across existing task, flow, subagent, session, and delivery owners, or keep any remaining recovery gaps within those owner-specific boundaries?
rationale: The patch is intentionally an RFC and does not establish whether the claimed cross-owner facts require a new core persistence contract; that architectural and upgrade-policy choice cannot be inferred safely from documentation wording alone.

options.title: Decline the shared layer for now
options.body: Keep lifecycle and recovery facts with existing owners unless a concrete missing generic core API is demonstrated.

options.title: Sponsor a narrower residual boundary
options.body: Name the exact cross-owner facts that cannot belong to a current owner, then require a bounded design and compatibility review before implementation.

options.title: Accept the proposed boundary
options.body: Adopt the ten-table residual contract as the intended core direction and assign an owner for the subsequent implementation and upgrade review.

recommendation.title: Decline the shared layer for now
recommendation.body: Keep lifecycle and recovery facts with existing owners unless a concrete missing generic core API is demonstrated.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR discussion specifically requests routing this owner-boundary decision to this person because of the stated Docs, Agent Reliability, and Runtime Hardening scope.
